## Simple explanation

Regression estimates a numeric quantity, such as a delivery time, energy
use, or house price. A model learns how input features relate to observed
numeric outcomes.

## Technical explanation

Regression specifies a function from predictors to a continuous target.
Linear regression models a weighted sum; nonlinear models can use trees,
neural networks, or other function classes. Losses such as mean squared
error estimate fit, while evaluation should use data not used to fit the
model.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Many systems need forecasts or numerical estimates rather than categories.
Model choice, feature quality, target definition, and error costs determine
whether regression outputs are useful for downstream decisions.

## How it works

The training procedure adjusts model parameters to reduce a loss between
predicted and observed targets. Engineers split data appropriately, inspect
residuals, compare against baselines, and check performance across relevant
ranges and subgroups.

## Practical example

A service can predict request latency from workload and resource features.
Evaluate errors on a later time period if deployment will predict future
traffic, and monitor for changes in workload distribution.

## Common misconceptions

- Regression is not synonymous with linear regression; many nonlinear
  models perform regression.
- A good average error can conceal large errors in important ranges or
  groups.
